g.text: One Trace, Twenty Services: Propagation Across Sync Calls and Async Queues
The async/queue hop is the one most systems get wrong -- no header exists to carry the context automatically
Synchronous chain -- HTTP headers carry the trace context, hop to hop
Async boundary -- the hard case: context rides IN the message, not a header
Span Collector Agents -- local per instance, batch + ship async, OFF the request's critical path
Query pattern is ALWAYS 'every span for trace X' --
the shard key that makes assembling one trace a single-shard read.
Waterfall UI reconstructs nesting from parent_span_id, not write order.
